items.title: Dan Morgenstern — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So that was my brief acquaintance with Pres.

ctx.x: my musician friends. But the fortunate thing was that he was recording for Atlantic, and Down Beat arranged for me to attend the session. He was recording with Coleman Hawkins, whom I had at that time already befriended. In fact, Coleman did a very big thing for me in terms of establishing me in the musicians’ circle. Coleman was known for never buying anybody a drink. It’s not that he was cheap, but he once explained it to me. He said, “You buy somebody a drink. Then they buy you one. You wind up drinking more…

was an experimenter. He got lost in his solo. So Lester went over to him, and he said – the Five Spot was a small club, and if you were sitting close to the band, you could hear – he said to Valdo – while he was playing, he said, “Don’t give up. Don’t ever give up.” It’s great. After this – the Five Spot, the old Five Spot, the original one, didn’t have a dressing room – the musicians – there was the kitchen, which wasn’t very busy. I don’t remember whether they had any food. I think that by law they were…
Dan, do you want to mention your early interview with Ornette Coleman?
